members.note: FString, not FText: the field edits a plain string and every road in and out of UUITextInput speaks one. Existing .dui authors it as a string.
FDreamTextInputStyle. Same role as FEditableTextBoxStyle, different shape: colours per state plus caret/selection/error, no Slate brushes.
GetHintText/SetHintText forward to it, so the UMG spelling reaches the same one string.
b-prefixed as every bool in this library is. Get/SetIsReadOnly carry the UMG spelling; the setter ends a live edit.
A two-valued enum here (Standard/Password) because the same field also carries PasswordChar. Get/SetIsPassword are the boolean spelling over it.
A floor under the control's own width and under what the paragraph asks a content-sized parent for. 0 = no opinion, which is every existing field.
Pushed to UUITextInput::bIsCaretMovedWhenGainFocus; only the activation nobody named a position for reads it.
The library's existing spelling of the same moment (an edit begins). Kept because .dui already authors it.

Read by UUITextInput::CancelInput, which is the road Back takes. Like UMG's RestoreOriginalText, the revert is committed once with the restored text (OnTextCommitted; the commit method is not exposed here). Two differences: the restore also fires OnTextChanged, because the `<->` reverse route rides OnValueChangedBP and a silent restore would leave bound models holding the abandoned edit; and the edit ends, because Escape is Back here. Off by default, as UMG's is and as the field behaved before.
Default TRUE where UMG's is false: Enter has always ended the edit here, and a default that changed existing screens is not a default.
Only acts when the commit kept the edit going; selecting a field nobody is editing shows a highlight with no caret.
Already existed; now carries a setter that closes a menu already open.
Same TEnumAsByte<EVirtualKeyboardType::Type>. Default means 'derive it from InputType', which is what the field always did; any other value states it outright.
No Blueprint accessor: FVirtualKeyboardOptions has no BlueprintType, exactly as in UMG. Registered in _BlueprintWritableExceptions.json.
Default OnAllFocusEvents where UMG's is OnFocusByPointer: every activation used to raise the keyboard, and a pad user has no other way to type.
Default TextCommitOnDismiss, which is what the field did: Done submitted and so did cancelling out.
EDreamUITextParagraphHorizontalAlign rather than ETextJustify -- the library's one paragraph-alignment enum, same three answers. The placeholder follows it.

ETextOverflowPolicy, UMG's own enum, but it only speaks WHILE NOBODY IS EDITING. On an editable field the paragraph's EDreamUITextOverflowType is the line-mode switch itself (the wrap and the caret's visible window both read it), so the line mode owns it during an edit and the policy owns it in between. Clip is the default and is what every field does today.

The half that means something here: EDreamTextFlowDirection is UMG's TextFlowDirection, pushed onto the value, the hint AND the error message. UMG's other half, TextShapingMethod, has no home on a widget -- whether the shaper runs at all is decided when the plugin is compiled (WITH_HARFBUZZ), not per control.
Same name and moment; carries FString rather than FText, like the Text property it reports.
Same name and moment, without UMG's ETextCommit: that enum describes Slate input routing this control does not have, and a fake one would be a lie in the signature.
Returns FString; see the Text property.
Takes FString; see the Text property.
Forwards to SetPlaceholder, which re-pushes the style because whether the hint is awake is decided against the field's emptiness.
Writes the Error paragraph -- right-aligned over the field, asleep while there is no message, coloured by FDreamTextInputStyle::ErrorColor. An empty message is a clear, as UMG's is.
The boolean spelling over DisplayType.
Answers from the message, so a template with no Error node still knows it has one.
Pushes onto the typed text AND the placeholder.
Forwards to UUITextInput::SetOverflowPolicy, which is the one writer of the paragraph's overflow and the only place that knows whether the line mode or the policy is speaking right now.
Appearance lives in the style struct, so the colour moves through SetStyle or the project sheet. A second setter writing the inline struct would be silently inert whenever StyleSource is the sheet.

Slate's font cache loads typeface faces asynchronously and this policy says what to paint meanwhile. This library renders from its own font data assets (SDF atlas or FreeType render), which have no async face load to paint around.
Same reason as FontFacesLoadingPaintPolicy: there is no asynchronous face load to finish.
